Which survey numbers can be merged?

Survey numbers can be merged only when all of these hold: the same owner (or all joint owners agree), the parcels are geographically adjacent with a shared boundary, they are in the same block/ward/town, they share the same land classification, and none of them carries an encumbrance, litigation or encroachment.

What is Sub-Registrar?

SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, where a sale deed is registered. When a deed is registered there, its IGRS system raises the patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number. An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no operator code; the officer's own checks on extent and boundaries still apply.

Explain litigation and stay orders

- A court reference in the EC or revenue records (sample form "O.S. 145/2023",
  "W.P. 8890/2024") puts the application on "On Hold - Litigation".
- Record the court name, case number, case type, parties and whether a stay
  order is active. No SLA clock runs during a litigation hold.
- The application resumes only on stay vacation, a judgment in the applicant's
  favour, or a registered settlement between the parties; a fresh field visit
  may be required after clearance.

What are the rules for rejection reasons and resubmission process?

Common Rejection Reasons:

1. Incomplete Documents
   - Missing required documents (Sale Deed, EC, IDs)
   - Invalid or expired documents
   - Documents not properly attested

2. Area Mismatch
   - Area in Sale Deed does not match survey records
   - Sub-division area calculations incorrect
   - Total area of sub-divisions does not equal original survey area

3. Encroachment Issues
   - Encroachment detected during field visit
   - Boundary disputes with neighboring properties
   - Unauthorized construction on land

4. Litigation Flag
   - Ongoing court cases related to the property
   - Disputed ownership claims
   - Stay orders from court

5. Revenue Arrears
   - Pending property taxes
   - Outstanding dues on the survey number
   - Non-payment of water/electricity charges linked to property

6. Invalid Survey Number
   - Survey number does not exist in records

What are the rules for required documents for isd?

1. Sale Deed
   - Must be registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must contain buyer and seller details, survey number, area

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

What does a temporary subdivision number like 3/T1 mean?

When an ISD or MERGE application is processed, the Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) assigns a temporary number to each proposed parcel before final numbers are confirmed. The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split (0 if the parent survey has none yet); T stands for Temporary; the number after T is a sequence counter (1, 2, 3...) for each new parcel.

What are the rules for sub-division numbering rules?

When to Create Sub-Division:
- When a single survey number is partitioned into multiple parcels
- When ownership of part of a survey number is transferred
- When land is sold in parts requiring separate patta
- When inheritance division requires separate land records

Sub-Division Numbering Pattern:
Original Survey: 145
First Level Sub-Division: 145/1, 145/2, 145/3
Second Level Sub-Division: 145/1A, 145/1B, 145/2A, 145/2B
Third Level Sub-Division: 145/1A1, 145/1A2, 145/1B1

Sub-Division Numbering Examples:

Example 1: Simple Partition
Survey 145 (1000 sq.m) divided into 2 parts
Result: 145/1 (600 sq.m), 145/2 (400 sq.m)

Example 2: Multiple Sub-Divisions
Survey 267 (2000 sq.m) divided into 4 parts
Result: 267/1 (500 sq.m), 267/2 (500 sq.m), 267/3 (600 sq.m), 267/4 (400 sq.m)

Example 3: Further Sub-Division

What does the SIS guide say about merge rules: which sub-divisions can be merged?

Survey Number Merging:
- Combines multiple survey numbers or sub-divisions into single survey number
- Used when adjacent land parcels are purchased by same owner
- Simplifies land records and patta management

Merge Eligibility Criteria:

1. Common Ownership
   - All survey numbers must have same owner
   - Ownership must be sole (not joint) or all joint owners must agree
   - Patta holder name must match across all surveys

2. Geographic Adjacency
   - Survey numbers must share common boundary
   - Non-adjacent surveys cannot be merged
   - At least one common boundary point required

3. Same Jurisdiction
   - All surveys must belong to same block
   - Surveys from different blocks cannot be merged
   - Surveys must be in same ward and town

4. Same Land Classification
   - All surveys must have same land type (agricultural, residential, commercial)

What are the rules for minimum extent and sub-division limits?

- Minimum measurable urban parcel: 1 sq.m; areas recorded to 2 decimal places
  in square metres. Extent may also be shown in ares (1 are = 100 sq.m).
- Sample minimum plot for a residential sub-division inside a corporation:
  300 sq.ft (~27.87 sq.m) frontage-permitting; local body building rules
  override where stricter.
- A sub-division that would leave any resulting parcel below the local minimum
  is refused; the applicant is asked to revise the partition.
- Maximum sub-division depth: 3 levels (145 -> 145/1 -> 145/1A -> 145/1A1).
  Beyond this the officer records a remark and refers to DIS.
- Sum of all sub-division extents MUST equal the parent survey extent within a
  tolerance of +/- 0.5%. Anything outside tolerance needs re-survey and a DIS
  variance note.

Explain sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

What are the rules for encroachment: regulatory treatment?

- Private-on-public encroachment (onto road, channel, tank) is reported to the
  local body; the application cannot be approved until the encroached extent is
  removed or regularised by the competent authority.
- Public-on-private and neighbour encroachment is recorded with measured extent
  and a sketch; the transfer may proceed only for the un-encroached extent
  unless the parties settle.
- An encroachment flag set at the field visit is visible to SD and blocks
  automatic approval; resolution typically extends the timeline by 15-30 days.

What does the SIS guide say about land type / classification codes?

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)

- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.

  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

Explain merge rules: which sub-divisions can be merged

Survey Number Merging:
- Combines multiple survey numbers or sub-divisions into single survey number
- Used when adjacent land parcels are purchased by same owner
- Simplifies land records and patta management

Merge Eligibility Criteria:

1. Common Ownership
   - All survey numbers must have same owner
   - Ownership must be sole (not joint) or all joint owners must agree
   - Patta holder name must match across all surveys

2. Geographic Adjacency
   - Survey numbers must share common boundary
   - Non-adjacent surveys cannot be merged
   - At least one common boundary point required

3. Same Jurisdiction
   - All surveys must belong to same block
   - Surveys from different blocks cannot be merged
   - Surveys must be in same ward and town

4. Same Land Classification
   - All surveys must have same land type (agricultural, residential, commercial)

What are the rules for sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means?

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

What does the SIS guide say about nisd workflow?

Step 1: Application Submission
- Service Code: 0153 (NISD - Not Involving Sub-Division)
- Application submitted through CSC, Sub-Registrar, or citizen portal
- Application number format: NISD/DISTRICT_CODE/YEAR/SEQUENCE
- No new sub-divisions are created, only ownership transfer

The NISD chain is short: application (CSC / citizen / Sub-Registrar) -> SIS
-> Zonal Level Tahsildar. There is no Senior Draughtsman (SD) step and no
Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) step - those belong to the ISD chain only.

Step 2: SIS Officer Verification
- SIS officer verifies documents: Sale Deed, EC (Encumbrance Certificate), Photo ID
- Officer checks if survey number exists and area matches records
- Officer verifies there are no pending disputes or litigation
- No field visit required unless specific issues are flagged
- Officer forwards the verified report directly to the Zonal Level Tahsildar

Explain survey number naming convention

Survey Number Structure:
- Survey numbers are unique identifiers for land parcels within a block
- Format: Numeric (e.g., 145, 267, 1023) or Alphanumeric (e.g., 145A, 267B)
- Each survey number belongs to exactly one block
- Survey numbers cannot be duplicated within the same block
- Survey numbers are permanent and do not change unless merged

Survey Number Components:
- Base Number: Primary identifier (e.g., 145)
- Optional Suffix: Letter suffix for related parcels (e.g., 145A, 145B)
- Block Association: Each survey number is linked to a specific block
- Ward Association: Block is part of a ward
- Town Association: Ward is part of a town

Example Hierarchy:
District: Chennai
  ↳ Taluk: Mylapore
    ↳ Town: T. Nagar
      ↳ Ward: Ward 5
        ↳ Block: Block 12
          ↳ Survey Numbers: 145, 146, 147, 148A, 148B

What are the rules for ownership record: what is held per owner?

Ownership of a survey number / sub-division is held as one row per owner, so a
jointly held parcel simply has several owner rows. For each owner the register
keeps: name (English and Tamil), the father's / husband's name with the
relationship (s/o, w/o, d/o), gender, address, the last four digits of the
Aadhaar number, and the ownership share. Two or more owner rows on the same
survey number means the parcel is jointly owned; a single row means a sole
owner.

The register does NOT hold an owner's mobile number, ration card number,
voter ID (EPIC), PIN code, occupation code or door number - those columns are
blank in the source extracts and are not projected. A question about one of
them is answered as "not recorded", not treated as missing data.

Explain minimum extent and sub-division limits

- Minimum measurable urban parcel: 1 sq.m; areas recorded to 2 decimal places
  in square metres. Extent may also be shown in ares (1 are = 100 sq.m).
- Sample minimum plot for a residential sub-division inside a corporation:
  300 sq.ft (~27.87 sq.m) frontage-permitting; local body building rules
  override where stricter.
- A sub-division that would leave any resulting parcel below the local minimum
  is refused; the applicant is asked to revise the partition.
- Maximum sub-division depth: 3 levels (145 -> 145/1 -> 145/1A -> 145/1A1).
  Beyond this the officer records a remark and refers to DIS.
- Sum of all sub-division extents MUST equal the parent survey extent within a
  tolerance of +/- 0.5%. Anything outside tolerance needs re-survey and a DIS
  variance note.

What are the rules for land type / classification codes?

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)
- 2 — Commercial / mixed use
- 3 — Industrial
- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

Rules that follow:
- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.
- Poramboke (type 5) cannot be sub-divided or transferred to a private owner
  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

What are the rules for survey number naming convention?

Survey Number Structure:
- Survey numbers are unique identifiers for land parcels within a block
- Format: Numeric (e.g., 145, 267, 1023) or Alphanumeric (e.g., 145A, 267B)
- Each survey number belongs to exactly one block
- Survey numbers cannot be duplicated within the same block
- Survey numbers are permanent and do not change unless merged

Survey Number Components:
- Base Number: Primary identifier (e.g., 145)
- Optional Suffix: Letter suffix for related parcels (e.g., 145A, 145B)
- Block Association: Each survey number is linked to a specific block
- Ward Association: Block is part of a ward
- Town Association: Ward is part of a town

Explain temporary subdivision numbers

When an ISD application is processed, the Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS)
assigns temporary subdivision numbers to each proposed parcel before the
final numbers are confirmed.

Format: {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}
- The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split
  (0 when the parent survey has no prior subdivision)
- T stands for "Temporary"
- The number after T is a sequence counter (1, 2, 3...) for each new parcel

Examples from real applications:

  Application 2022/0154/28/002277, survey 24, existing subdivision 3:
    Temp 3/T1 (12.2 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 3  (retains existing)
    Temp 3/T2 (27.8 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 4  (new number)

  Application 2023/0154/28/002278, survey 90, no prior subdivision:
    Temp 0/T1 (3.5 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 1
    Temp 0/T2 (3.5 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 2

What are the rules for isd workflow?

Step 1: Application Submission
- Service Code: 0154 (ISD - Involving Sub-Division)
- Applications can be submitted through CSC centers, Sub-Registrar offices, or directly by citizens
- Application receives a unique tracking number (format: ISD/DISTRICT_CODE/YEAR/SEQUENCE)
- All required documents must be uploaded at the time of submission

Step 2: SIS Officer Assignment
- Application is automatically assigned to the SIS officer based on jurisdiction (District/Taluk/Town/Ward/Block)
- Officer receives notification within 24 hours
- Application appears in officer's pending queue

Step 3: SIS Field Visit
- Officer must schedule field visit within 15 working days from application submission
- Field visit is mandatory for all ISD applications

What does the temporary number format mean?

For example, 3/T1 means "first temporary parcel from existing subdivision 3", and 0/T2 means "second temporary parcel from a survey with no prior subdivision".

Explain how the submission channel is decided

Every application carries a submission channel - CSC, citizen or sub_registrar.
It is read off two columns of urban_application_log, and nothing else:

- source_name is "-" (no operator account touched the file): the application
  came in unattended from the Sub-Registrar, where IGRS raised the mutation off
  the registered deed. Channel = sub_registrar.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code (samples "tut_tct_t131_02",
  "TNEFATUT0540-01") AND camp_flag = "P": the file was keyed in at a special
  revenue camp, where the operator enters it for the citizen standing in front
  of them. The submission is the citizen's own. Channel = citizen.
- source_name holds an operator or VLE code with any other camp_flag (blank,
  "S", "U", "Y"): keyed in at a Common Service Centre counter.
  Channel = CSC.

What are the rules for nisd workflow?

Step 1: Application Submission
- Service Code: 0153 (NISD - Not Involving Sub-Division)
- Application submitted through CSC, Sub-Registrar, or citizen portal
- Application number format: NISD/DISTRICT_CODE/YEAR/SEQUENCE
- No new sub-divisions are created, only ownership transfer

The NISD chain is short: application (CSC / citizen / Sub-Registrar) -> SIS
-> Zonal Level Tahsildar. There is no Senior Draughtsman (SD) step and no
Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) step - those belong to the ISD chain only.

Step 2: SIS Officer Verification
- SIS officer verifies documents: Sale Deed, EC (Encumbrance Certificate), Photo ID
- Officer checks if survey number exists and area matches records
- Officer verifies there are no pending disputes or litigation
- No field visit required unless specific issues are flagged
- Officer forwards the verified report directly to the Zonal Level Tahsildar

What does the SIS guide say about minimum extent and sub-division limits?

- Minimum measurable urban parcel: 1 sq.m; areas recorded to 2 decimal places
  in square metres. Extent may also be shown in ares (1 are = 100 sq.m).
- Sample minimum plot for a residential sub-division inside a corporation:
  300 sq.ft (~27.87 sq.m) frontage-permitting; local body building rules
  override where stricter.
- A sub-division that would leave any resulting parcel below the local minimum
  is refused; the applicant is asked to revise the partition.
- Maximum sub-division depth: 3 levels (145 -> 145/1 -> 145/1A -> 145/1A1).
  Beyond this the officer records a remark and refers to DIS.
- Sum of all sub-division extents MUST equal the parent survey extent within a
  tolerance of +/- 0.5%. Anything outside tolerance needs re-survey and a DIS
  variance note.

- Completed statuses: "approved", "rejected"
- Once an application reaches a completed status, a new application can be submitted for that survey number

What does the SIS guide say about sro, the can number, and what an absent igrs number means?

SRO stands for Sub-Registrar Office - the registration office where a sale deed
is registered. Officers say "SRO", "Sub-Registrar" and "sub registrar" for the
same office. When a deed is registered there, the SRO's IGRS system raises the
patta mutation off the registered document and issues an IGRS Form 6 number.
An application that reaches the SIS desk that way carries that number and no
operator code, and its submission channel is sub_registrar.

CAN stands for Citizen Access Number: the unique identity number a citizen is
issued and quotes on an application. most applications carry one.

Which applications carry an IGRS Form 6 number:

- A Sub-Registrar (SRO) referral always carries one. It names the registered
  deed the mutation was raised from, and its value is the same as that
  application's CAN number.
- A CSC application never carries one.

3. Revenue Dispute
   - Property tax assessment dispute
   - Land classification dispute (agricultural vs. residential)

   - Land grab cases

This application has no IGRS Form 6 number - what does that mean? Is it not from the SRO?

Correct - it did not come from the SRO. SRO is the Sub-Registrar Office, and only its IGRS system issues an IGRS Form 6 number, raised off the registered deed. An application without one was filed at a CSC counter or by the citizen at a revenue camp. What does the SIS guide say about important business rules?

Survey Number Application Rules:
- Only ONE active application (pending/in_progress) is allowed per survey number at any time
- A new application for the same survey number can ONLY be submitted AFTER the previous application is completed (approved or rejected)
- This rule applies to all application types: ISD, NISD, and MERGE
- Attempting to submit a duplicate application while one is pending will be rejected
- Officers should verify no active applications exist for a survey number before processing new submissions

Application Status Definitions:
- Active statuses: "pending", "in_progress", "escalated"
- Completed statuses: "approved", "rejected"
- Once an application reaches a completed status, a new application can be submitted for that survey number

Explain required documents for isd

1. Sale Deed
   - Must be registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must contain buyer and seller details, survey number, area

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

Explain sub-division numbering rules

When to Create Sub-Division:
- When a single survey number is partitioned into multiple parcels
- When ownership of part of a survey number is transferred
- When land is sold in parts requiring separate patta
- When inheritance division requires separate land records

Sub-Division Numbering Pattern:
Original Survey: 145
First Level Sub-Division: 145/1, 145/2, 145/3
Second Level Sub-Division: 145/1A, 145/1B, 145/2A, 145/2B
Third Level Sub-Division: 145/1A1, 145/1A2, 145/1B1

Sub-Division Numbering Examples:

Example 1: Simple Partition
Survey 145 (1000 sq.m) divided into 2 parts
Result: 145/1 (600 sq.m), 145/2 (400 sq.m)

Example 2: Multiple Sub-Divisions
Survey 267 (2000 sq.m) divided into 4 parts
Result: 267/1 (500 sq.m), 267/2 (500 sq.m), 267/3 (600 sq.m), 267/4 (400 sq.m)

Example 3: Further Sub-Division

Explain CSC

What does the SIS guide say about survey number naming convention?

Survey Number Structure:
- Survey numbers are unique identifiers for land parcels within a block
- Format: Numeric (e.g., 145, 267, 1023) or Alphanumeric (e.g., 145A, 267B)
- Each survey number belongs to exactly one block
- Survey numbers cannot be duplicated within the same block
- Survey numbers are permanent and do not change unless merged

Survey Number Components:
- Base Number: Primary identifier (e.g., 145)
- Optional Suffix: Letter suffix for related parcels (e.g., 145A, 145B)
- Block Association: Each survey number is linked to a specific block
- Ward Association: Block is part of a ward
- Town Association: Ward is part of a town

Example Hierarchy:
District: Chennai
  ↳ Taluk: Mylapore
    ↳ Town: T. Nagar
      ↳ Ward: Ward 5
        ↳ Block: Block 12
          ↳ Survey Numbers: 145, 146, 147, 148A, 148B

1. Incomplete Documents
   - Missing required documents (Sale Deed, EC, IDs)
   - Invalid or expired documents
   - Documents not properly attested

2. Area Mismatch
   - Area in Sale Deed does not match survey records
   - Sub-division area calculations incorrect
   - Total area of sub-divisions does not equal original survey area

3. Encroachment Issues
   - Encroachment detected during field visit
   - Boundary disputes with neighboring properties
   - Unauthorized construction on land

4. Litigation Flag
   - Ongoing court cases related to the property
   - Disputed ownership claims
   - Stay orders from court

5. Revenue Arrears
   - Pending property taxes
   - Outstanding dues on the survey number
   - Non-payment of water/electricity charges linked to property

6. Invalid Survey Number
   - Survey number does not exist in records

When to Create Sub-Division:
- When a single survey number is partitioned into multiple parcels
- When ownership of part of a survey number is transferred
- When land is sold in parts requiring separate patta
- When inheritance division requires separate land records

Sub-Division Numbering Pattern:
Original Survey: 145
First Level Sub-Division: 145/1, 145/2, 145/3
Second Level Sub-Division: 145/1A, 145/1B, 145/2A, 145/2B
Third Level Sub-Division: 145/1A1, 145/1A2, 145/1B1

Sub-Division Numbering Examples:

Example 1: Simple Partition
Survey 145 (1000 sq.m) divided into 2 parts
Result: 145/1 (600 sq.m), 145/2 (400 sq.m)

Example 2: Multiple Sub-Divisions
Survey 267 (2000 sq.m) divided into 4 parts
Result: 267/1 (500 sq.m), 267/2 (500 sq.m), 267/3 (600 sq.m), 267/4 (400 sq.m)

Example 3: Further Sub-Division

What are the rules for litigation flag process?

What is Litigation:
- Ongoing court case related to survey land
- Ownership dispute between multiple parties
- Boundary dispute with neighboring survey
- Stay order from civil or revenue court
- Criminal case involving land fraud or forgery

Types of Litigation:

1. Title Dispute
   - Multiple parties claiming ownership
   - Inherited property dispute
   - Will contest
   - Adverse possession claim

2. Boundary Dispute
   - Disagreement on survey boundaries
   - Conflicting survey documents
   - Encroachment dispute with neighbor

3. Revenue Dispute
   - Property tax assessment dispute
   - Land classification dispute (agricultural vs. residential)
   - Revenue recovery proceedings

4. Criminal Litigation
   - Land grab cases
   - Document forgery
   - Fraudulent sale deed
   - Impersonation

What does the SIS guide say about required documents for isd?

1. Sale Deed
   - Must be registered with Sub-Registrar
   - Original scan copy required
   - Must contain buyer and seller details, survey number, area

2. Encumbrance Certificate (EC)
   - Shows clear title for past 13 years
   - Must be obtained from Sub-Registrar office
   - Valid for 3 months from issue date

3. Survey Sketch
   - Existing survey sketch from revenue records
   - Shows current survey number and boundaries
   - Can be obtained from Tahsildar office

4. Photo ID
   - Aadhaar card (mandatory)
   - Additional ID: Driving License, Voter ID, Passport (any one)
   - Both buyer and seller photo IDs required

5. Photographs
   - Current photographs of the property
   - Boundary stone photographs (if applicable)
   - Minimum 4 photographs from different angles

What are the rules for temporary subdivision numbers?

When an ISD application is processed, the Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS)
assigns temporary subdivision numbers to each proposed parcel before the
final numbers are confirmed.

Format: {existing_subdivision}/T{sequence}
- The part before /T is the existing subdivision being split
  (0 when the parent survey has no prior subdivision)
- T stands for "Temporary"
- The number after T is a sequence counter (1, 2, 3...) for each new parcel

Examples from real applications:

  Application 2022/0154/28/008114, survey 24, existing subdivision 3:
    Temp 3/T1 (12.2 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 3  (retains existing)
    Temp 3/T2 (27.8 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 4  (new number)

  Application 2023/0154/28/008115, survey 90, no prior subdivision:
    Temp 0/T1 (3.5 sq.m) → Final subdivision number: 1

Explain nisd workflow

Step 1: Application Submission
- Service Code: 0153 (NISD - Not Involving Sub-Division)
- Application submitted through CSC, Sub-Registrar, or citizen portal
- Application number format: NISD/DISTRICT_CODE/YEAR/SEQUENCE
- No new sub-divisions are created, only ownership transfer

The NISD chain is short: application (CSC / citizen / Sub-Registrar) -> SIS
-> Zonal Level Tahsildar. There is no Senior Draughtsman (SD) step and no
Deputy Inspector Surveyor (DIS) step - those belong to the ISD chain only.

Step 2: SIS Officer Verification
- SIS officer verifies documents: Sale Deed, EC (Encumbrance Certificate), Photo ID
- Officer checks if survey number exists and area matches records
- Officer verifies there are no pending disputes or litigation
- No field visit required unless specific issues are flagged
- Officer forwards the verified report directly to the Zonal Level Tahsildar

Explain land type / classification codes

The land type code on a parcel controls what verification the SIS must do.
Sample mapping used in the urban extracts:

- 1 — Residential (நடைமுறை குடியிருப்பு)
- 2 — Commercial / mixed use
- 3 — Industrial
- 4 — Agricultural (wet / dry) inside town limits
- 5 — Government poramboke (road, channel, tank, burial ground)
- 6 — Institutional (temple, church, mosque, trust, educational)
- 7 — Vacant / unclassified

Rules that follow:
- A sub-division that changes land type (e.g. agricultural to residential) needs
  reclassification BEFORE the ISD sketch is finalised.
- Poramboke (type 5) cannot be sub-divided or transferred to a private owner
  except through a settlement service code (0179 / 0183) with the sanctioning GO
  quoted.
- Institutional land (type 6) transfer needs the endorsement of the controlling
  authority (HR&CE, Wakf Board, Diocese, or trust) on record.

  • What it is: a patta transfer that does not create a new subdivision, so no field visit and no SD sketch.
  • Workflow: Citizen / CSC / Sub-Registrar → SIS (document verification) → Zonal Level Tahsildar (DSC signature, order generated).
  • Fee: Government ₹100.00 + CSC charge ₹60.00.
  • SLA: 15-20 working days.
  • Field visit: not required.
